questions: Why does mRNA, rather than DNA itself, leave the nucleus?
What is built at the ribosome, and from what instructions?
segments.say: Central dogma: DNA makes protein. Narrate transcription in the nucleus, then follow the mRNA out to a ribosome for translation. Keep your student notes open at the DNA and gene definitions for this scene.

questions: Why is the genotype ratio 1:2:1 when the phenotype ratio is 3:1?
What is the chance that a child of Aa x Aa is a carrier?
segments.say: Monohybrid cross: the 3:1 ratio. Build the Aa x Aa square box by box, count genotypes 1:2:1 first, then group them into the 3:1 phenotypes. Now try the carrier-cross question on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: What must be true of the two genes for the 9:3:3:1 ratio to hold?
How many of the sixteen boxes show both recessive traits?
segments.say: Dihybrid cross: 9:3:3:1. Add a second gene on a different chromosome and count the sixteen boxes into four classes. Check the worked example in your student notes before attempting the dihybrid worksheet question.

questions: Why can a father not pass haemophilia directly to his son?
What fraction of a carrier mother's daughters are expected to be carriers?
segments.say: Sex-linked inheritance. Track the X chromosomes from a carrier mother and a normal father, and show why sons are at risk while daughters become carriers. Finish the sex-linked question on the worksheet now.

questions: Give one reason a mutation can be neutral.
In one sentence, what do a rare few mutations provide for evolution?
segments.say: A common mistake: mutations are always harmful. Strike through the trap claim, then show the mutated gene still building a working protein. Finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this scene.
segments.watchFor: Every mutation harms the organism. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the worksheet: any answer treating every sequence change as damage shows the trap reading - send them back to scene s5 and to the correct turn: Most mutations are neutral: only some are harmful, and a rare few are the raw material of evolution.
